research_question: Among people with Alzheimer's disease, what is the effect at 6 months of regular-release galantamine 16–24 mg/day (8–12 mg twice daily), compared with placebo, on cognitive function measured as change from baseline on the ADAS-cog?
treatment_label: Regular-release galantamine 16–24 mg/day (8–12 mg twice daily)
outcome_description: Cognitive function measured by ADAS-cog change from baseline at 6 months. Extract only the regular-release 16–24 mg/day dose arm and its corresponding placebo data; exclude 8 mg/day, prolonged-release 16–24 mg/day, and 32 mg/day dose arms. For multi-dose trials such as Tariot 2000 and Brodaty 2005, compare only the eligible 16–24 mg/day arm with the shared placebo group and do not include the other active-dose arms.
positive_direction: A positive pooled effect means that regular-release galantamine 16–24 mg/day produces greater cognitive improvement, or less cognitive deterioration, on ADAS-cog at 6 months than placebo.
search_queries: galantamine Alzheimer placebo controlled trial ADAS-cog
galantamine 16 24 mg Alzheimer cognitive outcome placebo
regular release galantamine twice daily Alzheimer quantitative comparison
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies enrolling people with Alzheimer's disease and including a regular-release galantamine 16–24 mg/day (8–12 mg twice-daily) arm and a placebo comparator.
Studies reporting ADAS-cog change from baseline at approximately 6 months for the eligible dose comparison.
Studies providing quantitative results sufficient to derive a mean difference and its sampling variance, including directly reported means and dispersion or convertible test statistics.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, and theoretical papers.
No comparison between the eligible regular-release galantamine 16–24 mg/day treatment arm and a placebo control condition.
No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as means with SDs, t/F-values, proportions, or odds ratios.

Completely unrelated to Alzheimer's disease, galantamine treatment, or the specified ADAS-cog outcome; this also excludes ineligible galantamine formulations or dose arms when no eligible regular-release 16–24 mg/day arm is reported.
moderators_to_extract: galantamine dose within the eligible range (16, 18, 20, or 24 mg/day)
trial duration and exact timing of the nominal 6-month assessment
analysis population (intention-to-treat, modified intention-to-treat, or completer)
method used to handle missing outcome data
effect_size_note: Pool the between-group mean difference in ADAS-cog change from baseline at 6 months using a common sign convention so positive values favor galantamine. Because higher ADAS-cog scores indicate worse cognition, reverse signs where necessary depending on how change was defined (follow-up minus baseline versus baseline minus follow-up). Use each eligible trial only once. In Tariot 2000, Brodaty 2005, and any other multi-arm trial, extract only the regular-release 16–24 mg/day arm and compare it with the shared placebo group; do not extract or combine the 8 mg/day, prolonged-release 16–24 mg/day, or 32 mg/day arms. Since only one eligible active arm per trial enters this meta-analysis, the shared placebo group should not be split.
single_outcome_target: cognitive function measured by ADAS-cog change from baseline at 6 months
